memory_update.text: Keep VRT as the reference benchmark for data-center power/cooling infrastructure, but do not let it crowd out smaller or less obvious suppliers in later layers.

POWL is a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the switchgear/electrical-room chokepoint because management has explicitly linked AI data-center development to medium-voltage switchgear opportunities.
MOD is a high-priority underfollowed thermal-management candidate because its 10-K directly maps product categories to high-density data-center cooling and discloses component supply constraints.
IESC should be tracked as an execution-capacity and custom electrical-infrastructure candidate, especially where skilled labor, field services, and project delivery become bottlenecks.

Need a later pass on sub-$10B or $300M-$1B names in conduit, busway, enclosures, PDUs, backup generation, test/commissioning, and niche liquid-cooling components; this pass found unusually direct exposure but most surfaced names have already moved into large-cap territory.

POWL should be tracked as a high-relevance underfollowed electrical bottleneck candidate because it has direct medium-voltage switchgear exposure and a disclosed data-center order exceeding $400 million.
MOD should be tracked as a data-center thermal-management candidate because the $4 billion hyperscale chiller agreement creates unusually direct evidence of AI/data-center cooling exposure.

NVT should be tracked as a liquid-cooling and power-distribution-adjacent candidate because it has deployed more than 2 GW of liquid-cooling capacity and participates in AI data-center reference architecture work.

Potential additional Layer 1B candidates not included due to the four-candidate limit: FIX for specialized MEP/data-center project execution, WCC for electrical distribution and transformers, and ATKR for conduit/cable-management components.

The node's investable chokepoints appear to split into at least four subnodes: liquid cooling/CDUs/manifolds, chillers and heat rejection, medium-voltage switchgear/electrical rooms, and specialized MEP integration/commissioning.

POWL should remain in the data-center power/switchgear lane; evidence is stronger after the disclosed >$400M data-center order and backlog expansion, but later layers must separate recurring exposure from lumpy mega-project risk.
MOD is a direct cooling-capacity candidate through Airedale by Modine; next research should quantify data-center revenue, backlog, liquid-cooling exposure, and customer concentration.
IESC is a lower-attention electrical/project-execution candidate; include as a hypothesis until SEC filings confirm data-center revenue mix, backlog, and customer dependency.

The most important evidence gap for this node is not product existence but capacity economics: lead times, backlog conversion, cancellation risk, customer concentration, and labor/project-execution bottlenecks.

NVT should be kept as a near-reference liquid-cooling and rack power-distribution name; not small-cap, but direct evidence includes NVIDIA collaboration, Siemens/NVIDIA reference architecture, Google OCP CDU work, and expanded manufacturing.

AAON/BASX is a high-priority underfollowed cooling candidate despite market cap slightly above $10B because BASX has explicit data-center liquid-cooling orders, backlog growth, and capacity expansion.
MOD/Airedale is a direct AI data-center cooling supplier with disclosed $180M AI infrastructure developer order and manufacturing expansion; verify repeatability and margin impact.
MEI is a speculative small-cap shadow candidate for data-center power-distribution products; keep only if filings confirm material AI/cloud power-distribution exposure and customer qualification.

Need a separate pass for electrical balance-of-plant names below $10B: switchgear, busway, enclosures, conduit, commissioning, testing, and specialty electrical contractors. Atkore and Powell surfaced but require more direct data-center/customer evidence before inclusion.
